name: MD-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+17 district lean gives Democrats a large structural advantage
Boafo's $1.9M raised and $12M in outside support versus no visible Republican funding
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%
Open seat after Hoyer's retirement is the main residual uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's 17-point Democratic lean, Boafo's decisive fundraising and outside-spending advantage, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 96% all point to a comfortable hold despite the open seat.
model.watch: A wave of Republican outside spending or a sharply favorable national environment could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat would still require an unusual shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Steny Hoyer (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Maryland's 5th District leans Democratic by 17 points and has long been held by Steny Hoyer, who is retiring. Adrian Boafo enters the general election as the clear Democratic favorite, backed by about $1.9 million in fundraising and more than $12 million in outside support, while Republican Chris Chaffee shows little visible financial activity.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the fundraising gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win near 96%. The open seat removes the incumbent's personal advantage, but the district's partisan lean is wide enough that even a well-funded Republican effort would need an unusual environment to close the gap. A Democratic hold is the expected outcome.
